question: Amlodipine belongs to which group of antihypertensive drugs?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. calcium channel blocker

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Amlodipine blocks the calcium channels in the smooth muscle of the blood vessels, which relaxes them and lowers the pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor: The angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors end in pril

B — diuretic: The diuretics act on the kidney and include thiazides and frusemide

C — beta blocker: The beta blockers end in lol and slow the heart

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is taught to take the drug at the same time every day and never to stop it on his own, since the pressure rises again quietly when it is stopped

question: A common side effect of nifedipine is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ankle oedema with flushing and headache

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The drug dilates the arterioles, so the ankles swell and the flushing and headache follow the sudden fall in the peripheral resistance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a dry cough: A dry cough is typical of the angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors

C — loss of hearing: Hearing loss is associated with some antibiotics and diuretics but not with nifedipine

D — a slow pulse: A slow pulse is seen with the beta blockers

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The swelling is not due to heart or kidney failure, and the patient is reassured while the doctor decides whether to change the drug

question: The insulin preparation that is given once daily, usually at bedtime, because of its long and steady action is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. insulin glargine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Insulin glargine is a long acting analogue with a nearly flat effect lasting about twenty four hours, so it provides the basal cover

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — regular insulin: Regular insulin acts within half an hour and lasts about six hours

C — isophane insulin: Isophane insulin is intermediate acting and is usually given twice a day

D — insulin lispro: Insulin lispro acts within fifteen minutes and covers a meal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dose of the long acting insulin is adjusted from the fasting blood sugar, while the rapid acting insulin is adjusted from the readings after meals

question: Regular (soluble) insulin given subcutaneously begins to act after about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 30 minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The onset is about half an hour, the peak at two to four hours and the duration about six hours

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 5 minutes: Five minutes is the onset of the rapid acting analogues given intravenously

B — 4 hours: Four hours is close to the time of the peak effect

C — 8 hours: Eight hours is beyond the duration of this preparation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: A meal must be ready within half an hour of the injection, otherwise the patient becomes hypoglycaemic before the food is absorbed

question: Which group of drugs is placed in the high alert category because an error in the dose can cause serious harm?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. insulin and heparin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Insulin and heparin have a narrow margin of safety, so an error of a decimal point can cause severe hypoglycaemia or bleeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin tablets: Vitamins are not high alert drugs

B — cough syrups: Cough syrups are not in this category

C — paracetamol and antacids: Paracetamol is safe in the usual doses and antacids have very few serious effects

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: High alert drugs are stored separately with a coloured label, are checked by two nurses and are never left unattended on a trolley

question: Look-alike and sound-alike drugs are those which:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. have similar names or packaging and are therefore easily confused

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The names or the labels resemble one another, so the wrong drug is picked up in a hurry, which is why such pairs are listed and stored apart

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — are always stored in the refrigerator: Storage conditions are not part of the definition

C — are always given by injection: The route of administration is unrelated to this problem

D — have the same colour: Colour alone is not the criterion, though similar packaging adds to the risk

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the label three times, once when taking the drug from the shelf, once before drawing it up and once before giving it, and confirms the indication with the prescription
option_2: have similar names or packaging and are therefore easily confused

question: An adverse drug reaction is best defined as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a harmful and unintended response to a drug given in the normal dose

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The reaction occurs even when the drug has been prescribed and given correctly, and it is unwanted and harmful

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an overdose taken by mistake: An overdose is a poisoning and not an adverse reaction in this sense

B — an error in the dose given by the nurse: A wrong dose is a medication error rather than an adverse reaction

D — the expected effect of the drug: The expected therapeutic effect is not a reaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Every suspected reaction is reported, however mild, since only a collected series of reports can bring out a rare effect that a single ward would never notice
option_2: an error in the dose given by the nurse
option_3: a harmful and unintended response to a drug given in the normal dose

question: The main aim of pharmacovigilance is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. detect, assess and prevent the harmful effects of medicines after they come into use

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Once a drug is in general use, the uncommon and delayed effects appear, and organised reporting brings them out so that advice and labels can be changed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — test new drugs on healthy volunteers: Testing on volunteers is done during clinical trials before approval

B — increase the sale of medicines: Promoting sales is a commercial activity and not the aim

D — fix the price of medicines: Pricing is the work of the pricing authority

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse is often the first person to notice the reaction, and a well filled report with the details of the drug and the timing is what makes it useful
option_3: detect, assess and prevent the harmful effects of medicines after they come into use

question: A 55-year-old man who has been taking enalapril for two months complains of a persistent dry cough that keeps him awake at night. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. record the complaint and report it, as the cough is a known effect of this group of drugs and the treatment may be changed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors commonly cause a dry cough, and the doctor may change the drug to another group of tablets

🔍 Key Clues: 55-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give him a cough syrup and continue the drug for ever: A cough syrup does not treat the cause and the patient continues to be troubled

C — ask him to stop the drug at once himself: Stopping the drug without advice may raise the blood pressure suddenly

D — reassure him and say that the cough is due to the weather: Dismissing the symptom leaves the patient to suffer a side effect that can easily be corrected

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: If the cough is accompanied by swelling of the face, the tongue or the throat, the drug is stopped at once and treated as an emergency
option_1: record the complaint and report it, as the cough is a known effect of this group of drugs and the treatment may be changed
option_2: give him a cough syrup and continue the drug for ever
option_3: ask him to stop the drug at once himself
option_4: reassure him and say that the cough is due to the weather

question: A patient taking a thiazide diuretic for high blood pressure should be advised to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. take it in the morning and include foods rich in potassium in the diet

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Taken in the morning, the diuresis occurs during the day and does not disturb sleep, and the potassium rich foods prevent a low potassium level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — take the tablet at bedtime: A dose at night means repeated visits to the toilet, which disturbs the patient and may cause a fall

B — stop the salt restriction now: Salt restriction continues to be important along with the drug

C — reduce the fluid intake to one glass a day: Reducing the fluid intake causes dehydration and does not lower the blood pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is asked to report muscle cramps and unusual weakness, which are the common symptoms of a low potassium level
option_3: reduce the fluid intake to one glass a day
option_4: take it in the morning and include foods rich in potassium in the diet

question: Insulin is best injected into the abdomen because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. absorption from the abdomen is the most rapid and the most consistent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The abdominal wall has a good blood supply and the rate of absorption is steady, though it is slightly slower when the injection is given near the umbilicus

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — it needs no rotation of sites: Sites must still be rotated to prevent fat lumps

C — it does not cause hypoglycaemia: Hypoglycaemia can occur with any site if the dose is high or a meal is missed

D — the injection is painless there: Pain is not the reason, although the fine needle makes the injection nearly painless anywhere

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Exercising the limb into which the insulin was injected speeds up absorption, which is why the patient is advised to keep the site and the activity constant
option_1: absorption from the abdomen is the most rapid and the most consistent

question: A 60-year-old man with diabetes who takes insulin becomes sweaty, shaky and confused half an hour after the injection and has not eaten his meal. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. recognise hypoglycaemia, give four teaspoons of glucose or sugar in water if he can swallow, recheck the sugar and delay the insulin dose until he has eaten

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the early features of hypoglycaemia, and quick sugar by mouth corrects them within minutes when the patient is conscious

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ask him to walk about to shake off the feeling: Exercise uses up more glucose and deepens the hypoglycaemia

C — give another dose of insulin: More insulin drives the sugar down further and may cause a fit or coma

D — give him a cup of tea without sugar: Tea without sugar contains no glucose and does not help

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: If the patient cannot swallow or is unconscious, glucose is given intravenously and never by mouth, since the fluid may be inhaled
option_1: recognise hypoglycaemia, give four teaspoons of glucose or sugar in water if he can swallow, recheck the sugar and delay the insulin dose until he has eaten
option_2: ask him to walk about to shake off the feeling
option_4: give him a cup of tea without sugar

question: Concentrated potassium chloride is treated as a high alert drug because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. an error in its dose or an undiluted injection can cause cardiac arrest

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rapid or undiluted injection of potassium stops the heart, and several deaths have followed this single mistake

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — it must be given with food: It is given intravenously and not with food

B — it has no therapeutic use: It is a valuable drug for treating a low potassium level

C — it is expensive: Cost is not the reason for the classification

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The concentrated ampoule is stored apart from other drugs with a clear warning label, is always diluted, and is given slowly through a pump with cardiac monitoring
option_4: an error in its dose or an undiluted injection can cause cardiac arrest

question: A 70-year-old woman on treatment for high blood pressure feels giddy when she stands up quickly, and her pressure is 96/64 mm Hg on standing. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. explain that this is postural hypotension, advise her to rise slowly in stages, to sit on the edge of the bed before standing and to report if it persists

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pressure falls on standing because of the drug and the reduced reflexes of age, and slow changes of posture with help prevent a fall

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old | 64 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a hot bath to improve the circulation: A hot bath dilates the vessels further and makes the giddiness worse

B — tell her that the giddiness is due to old age: Attributing the symptom to age leaves a treatable cause and a real risk of a fall unattended

D — ask her to stop the drug at once: Stopping the drug suddenly can raise the pressure dangerously

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Her pressure is recorded lying and standing at every visit, and the bathroom and the path from the bed are kept clear to prevent a fall
option_1: give her a hot bath to improve the circulation
option_2: tell her that the giddiness is due to old age
option_3: explain that this is postural hypotension, advise her to rise slowly in stages, to sit on the edge of the bed before standing and to report if it persists
option_4: ask her to stop the drug at once

question: A 65-year-old man on a diuretic for high blood pressure has a serum potassium of 2.9 milliequivalents per litre and complains of cramps and weakness. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. report the value at once, give the prescribed potassium supplement and encourage fruit, coconut water and green leafy vegetables as advised, and monitor the pulse and the muscle power

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low potassium level causes cramps, weakness and dangerous arrhythmias, and it is corrected by the prescribed supplement and a potassium rich diet

🔍 Key Clues: 65-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a double dose of the diuretic: Doubling the diuretic lowers the potassium further

C — restrict all fluids to correct the level: Fluid restriction has no effect on the potassium level

D — ignore the report, as the kidney will correct it: A level below three does not correct itself and can cause a fatal arrhythmia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The electrocardiogram is watched for flat T waves and prominent U waves, which are the signs of a low potassium level
option_1: give a double dose of the diuretic
option_2: report the value at once, give the prescribed potassium supplement and encourage fruit, coconut water and green leafy vegetables as advised, and monitor the pulse and the muscle power
option_3: restrict all fluids to correct the level

question: Which insulin preparation may be given by the intravenous route in an emergency?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. regular (soluble) insulin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Only the clear soluble insulin is given intravenously, in a saline infusion or by a pump, in ketoacidosis and in the perioperative period

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — insulin glargine: The long acting analogue is designed only for the subcutaneous route

B — a premixed insulin: A premixed preparation contains an intermediate acting component and is given subcutaneously only

D — isophane insulin: The intermediate acting cloudy preparation must not be given intravenously

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: When the patient begins to take food by mouth, he is switched back to the subcutaneous route before the infusion is stopped, otherwise the sugar rises again

question: Which adverse drug reaction requires the drug to be stopped immediately and reported at once?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. peeling of the skin with blisters and sores in the mouth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Widespread peeling of the skin with blisters and involvement of the mouth suggests a severe drug induced skin reaction, which can be fatal and calls for immediate withdrawal

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — slight drowsiness: Mild drowsiness is common at the start of treatment

B — a dry mouth: A dry mouth is a minor effect

D — mild nausea on the first day: Mild nausea may settle and does not need the drug to be stopped

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Warning the patient to report any rash early is far more useful than waiting for the reaction to become severe
option_3: peeling of the skin with blisters and sores in the mouth

question: Which of the following pairs of drugs is a well known look-alike and sound-alike pair?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. hydralazine and hydroxyzine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The two names are almost identical though one lowers the blood pressure and the other is an antihistamine, which is exactly what makes the pair dangerous

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — insulin and heparin: These do different things and their names are quite distinct

C — amoxicillin and ampicillin: These are two different antibiotics with similar names but they belong to the same group and are often used interchangeably

D — paracetamol and aspirin: These two names are clearly different, although both are painkillers

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The listed pairs are displayed on a chart in the ward, and the indication written on the prescription is checked before the drug is picked up

question: A 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes who takes insulin and a sulfonylurea tablet has repeated episodes of low blood sugar in the afternoon. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. record the timing and the readings of the low sugars, ensure that the mid afternoon snack is taken, and report so that the doses can be reviewed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Both the insulin and the sulfonylurea lower the sugar, and the pattern of the readings tells the doctor which dose to reduce

🔍 Key Clues: 58-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — advise him to sleep in the afternoon without eating: Sleeping without food in the afternoon allows the sugar to fall unnoticed

B — stop all food in the afternoon: Missing food is itself a cause of a low sugar

D — increase the insulin dose himself: Increasing the insulin deepens the hypoglycaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is taught to keep sugar or glucose with him at all times, and the family is shown how to give it if he becomes drowsy
option_1: advise him to sleep in the afternoon without eating
option_3: record the timing and the readings of the low sugars, ensure that the mid afternoon snack is taken, and report so that the doses can be reviewed

question: The correct way to store and prepare insulin is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keep the in use vial in the refrigerator or a cool place, never freeze it, and roll it gently between the palms before drawing the dose

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Insulin loses its strength if it freezes or gets too warm, and rolling mixes the cloudy preparation without causing froth

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep it in direct sunlight on the window sill: Sunlight and heat destroy the insulin

B — shake the vial vigorously before use: Vigorous shaking produces froth and makes the dose inaccurate

C — keep the vial in the freezer and use it when frozen: A frozen vial must be discarded, as the protein is destroyed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The vial in use may be kept at room temperature for about a month, but the spare stock is always kept in the refrigerator between two and eight degrees

question: Beta blockers are given cautiously to a patient with asthma because they may cause:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. narrowing of the airways with wheezing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Blocking the beta receptors in the lungs allows the bronchial muscle to constrict, which brings on wheezing and breathlessness in a patient with asthma

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a rise in the blood sugar: The blood sugar is affected by other drugs and this is not the main concern here

B — loss of vision: Loss of vision is not a typical effect of this group

C — bleeding from the gums: Bleeding from the gums is not caused by them

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Even the eye drops used for glaucoma can be absorbed and cause wheezing, so the drug and its route are both reviewed in a patient with asthma

question: A 40-year-old woman taking a diuretic for high blood pressure becomes confused, and her serum sodium is 128 milliequivalents per litre. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. report the value at once, restrict the fluids as ordered, monitor the level of consciousness and the sodium, and record the intake and output accurately

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sodium level of one hundred and twenty eight with confusion needs prompt correction under supervision, and the fluid restriction and accurate recording guide the treatment

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a large quantity of water to correct the confusion: Extra water dilutes the sodium further and can cause a fit

C — give her extra salt at once without an order: Salt is not given without a medical order and the correction must be slow

D — ignore the report, as the value is close to normal: The value is below the normal range and the patient already has symptoms

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The sodium is corrected slowly, since a rapid rise can damage the brain, and the patient is watched for drowsiness, headache and convulsions
option_1: give her a large quantity of water to correct the confusion

question: Gas gangrene is caused by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Clostridium perfringens

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The organism grows in the absence of oxygen in a deep wound and produces toxins and gas that destroy the muscle

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Staphylococcus aureus: Staphylococcus aureus causes abscesses and wound infection with pus

C — Streptococcus pyogenes: Streptococcus pyogenes causes cellulitis and a spreading infection of the skin

D — Escherichia coli: Escherichia coli causes urinary and bowel infections

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Wide opening and cleaning of the wound removes the oxygen free environment on which the organism depends, which is why surgery is the first step

question: A patient brings a deep, dirty wound from a road accident in which the skin is broken and there is a foul smell with crackling under the skin on pressing. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. treat it as an anaerobic infection, keep the wound open and covered with a sterile dressing, start the prescribed antibiotics and arrange urgent surgical review

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Crackling under the skin and a foul smell point to gas forming organisms, and early surgical debridement with antibiotics is what saves the limb and the life

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — apply a hot fomentation and review after a week: Delay allows the infection to spread along the muscle planes and cause shock

B — apply a tight dressing and send the patient home: A tight dressing closes the wound and favours the growth of the anaerobes

D — irrigate the wound with an antiseptic and close it with sutures: Closing such a wound traps the organisms deep inside

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is also given tetanus toxoid and watched for a rising pulse, falling blood pressure and increasing pain, which indicate a spreading infection
option_1: apply a hot fomentation and review after a week
option_2: apply a tight dressing and send the patient home
option_3: treat it as an anaerobic infection, keep the wound open and covered with a sterile dressing, start the prescribed antibiotics and arrange urgent surgical review

question: The method used in the laboratory to demonstrate the motility of bacteria is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the hanging drop preparation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A drop of the broth culture is suspended on a cover slip over a cavity slide and the moving organisms are seen under the microscope against a dark background

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the Gram stain: The Gram stain shows the shape and the staining character but not the movement

B — the Ziehl-Neelsen stain: The Ziehl-Neelsen stain is used for acid fast bacilli

C — the Widal test: The Widal test detects antibodies in the serum

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The preparation is examined at once and with a reduced light, since the organisms stop moving when the drop begins to dry

question: The immunoglobulin that is present in the secretions of the mucous membranes and in breast milk is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. immunoglobulin A

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Immunoglobulin A protects the mucosal surfaces of the gut, the airway and the genital tract and is passed to the baby in the colostrum

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — immunoglobulin G: Immunoglobulin G crosses the placenta and gives the newborn protection for the first few months

B — immunoglobulin M: Immunoglobulin M appears first in a new infection

C — immunoglobulin E: Immunoglobulin E is involved in allergic reactions and in worm infestation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The protection given by breast milk acts on the lining of the baby's gut, which is why it reduces diarrhoea and respiratory infection even in a community with poor sanitation

question: A blood sample is sent to the laboratory for a Widal test from a patient who has had a step ladder fever for ten days with a slow pulse and a coated tongue. The test is used to detect:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. antibodies formed against the organism in the patient's serum

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Widal test measures the antibodies that the patient has produced against Salmonella typhi, and the level rises in the second week of the illness

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the number of white cells in the blood: The total white cell count is a separate test on the same sample

C — the organism in the blood: The organism is demonstrated by a blood culture, which is most useful in the first week

D — the toxin produced by the organism: The toxin is not detected by this test

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The result is read with the clinical picture, since a previous infection or immunisation can also raise the level
option_1: antibodies formed against the organism in the patient's serum
option_2: the number of white cells in the blood

question: Used culture plates in the laboratory are disposed of by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. decontaminating them by autoclaving before they are discarded

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The plates carry a heavy growth of organisms, so they are sterilised in the autoclave before the material is removed and thrown away

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — throwing them into the ordinary bin: An ordinary bin allows the organisms to spread to the staff and the surroundings

B — keeping them on the bench for the next day: Plates left on the bench dry out, become airborne and are a hazard

D — washing them in running water and reusing them without treatment: Washing without treatment contaminates the sink and the hands of the worker

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: All the infectious waste of the hospital receives the same treatment, since sharps, cultures and infected dressings can all transmit infection to the staff who handle them
option_2: keeping them on the bench for the next day
option_3: decontaminating them by autoclaving before they are discarded

question: The correct order in the laboratory investigation of a specimen is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. direct microscopy, culture of the specimen, identification of the organism and then the sensitivity test

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The specimen is examined first under the microscope, then cultured to grow the organism, which is identified and finally tested against antibiotics

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — culture, sensitivity, microscopy: Microscopy comes first, since it gives an immediate clue and may show the organism at once

B — sensitivity test, culture, microscopy: The sensitivity cannot be done before the organism is grown

C — identification, microscopy, culture, sensitivity: Identification requires the organism to be grown first and follows the culture

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The Gram stain report from the direct microscopy often allows a suitable antibiotic to be started while the culture is awaited
option_4: direct microscopy, culture of the specimen, identification of the organism and then the sensitivity test

question: A patient who had an operation a week ago has a discharging wound, and the culture grows Staphylococcus aureus that is resistant to methicillin. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. nurse the patient in a single room if available, use contact precautions with gloves and gown, wash the hands before and after care, and follow the antibiotic sensitivity report for treatment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This organism spreads by contact from the hands and the clothing of the staff, so isolation along with hand hygiene breaks the chain of transmission

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — allow the patient to move about the whole ward freely: Free movement of such a patient spreads the organism through the whole ward

B — treat the wound with a dressing only and take no other step: A dressing alone allows the infection to spread to other patients

question: The most important single measure to prevent infection among the staff and the patients in a hospital laboratory is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. washing the hands before and after every procedure and following standard precautions

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hand hygiene at the right moments and the standard precautions break the chain of contact spread, which is the commonest route in a laboratory

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — wearing a laboratory coat all day: A coat alone gives no protection against organisms on the hands

B — using a separate pen for every sample: The pen is not a recognised route of spread, unlike the hands

D — keeping the windows closed: Ventilation is useful but is not the main measure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Gloves are worn for every procedure involving blood or body fluids, but they never replace hand washing after the gloves are removed

option_3: washing the hands before and after every procedure and following standard precautions

question: Healing by first intention occurs in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a clean surgical wound whose edges are held together

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the edges are approximated and there is no infection or tissue loss, the wound heals quickly with a thin scar

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a wound left open to heal: A wound left open heals by secondary intention and leaves a wide scar

C — an infected wound with pus: An infected wound heals by secondary intention after the pus has drained

D — a burn with loss of skin: A burn with skin loss heals by secondary intention with granulation tissue

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The sutured wound is kept clean and dry, since an infection converts a first intention healing into a secondary one and leaves an ugly scar

question: The commonest organisms responsible for an abscess are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the pyogenic bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pus forming bacteria, of which Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest, attract neutrophils and produce an abscess

❌ Why Not Other Options?

C — Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Tuberculosis produces a chronic granuloma with caseous material rather than an acute abscess

D — the viruses: Viruses do not produce pus

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

option_2: the pyogenic bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus

question: A 50-year-old man has a soft, painless, freely movable swelling under the skin of his forearm, and the aspirate shows fat cells. The most likely diagnosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a benign fatty tumour

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a malignant tumour of the fat: A malignant fatty tumour is rare, grows rapidly and is usually fixed and deep

B — a cyst: A cyst yields clear or cheesy material and not fat cells

D — an abscess: An abscess is warm, tender and fluctuant and yields pus on aspiration

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is reassured, and surgical removal is advised only if the swelling is large, painful or growing quickly

question: The cardinal signs of acute inflammation are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. redness, heat, swelling, pain and loss of function

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The increased blood flow and the leak of fluid and cells produce these five classical signs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a hard fixed swelling: A hard, fixed swelling suggests a tumour

question: Which finding suggests that a tumour has spread to a lymph node?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a hard, enlarged and fixed node that does not regress

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Malignant cells grow within the node, which becomes firm, enlarged and fixed to the surrounding tissue, and it does not subside

question: A 60-year-old man who has had pain in the upper abdomen for months is found to have a gastric ulcer, and the biopsy report shows a malignant change. The nurse should:
solution:

question: An anaphylactic reaction to a drug is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. immediate or type I hypersensitivity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The drug combines with the immunoglobulin E on the mast cells, which release histamine and produce the swelling, the wheezing and the fall in blood pressure within minutes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an autoimmune disease: Autoimmunity is directed against the body's own tissues and is not involved here

B — a direct toxic effect of the drug: A toxic effect follows a large dose and does not need the immune system

C — delayed or type IV hypersensitivity: Delayed hypersensitivity develops over one to three days and takes the form of a contact dermatitis

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Adrenaline must be at hand whenever an injection that can cause this reaction is given, and the allergy is recorded prominently in the case sheet
option_2: a direct toxic effect of the drug

question: The main reason for anaemia in a patient with chronic kidney disease is a deficiency of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. erythropoietin produced by the kidney

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The damaged kidney makes too little erythropoietin, so the marrow is not stimulated to produce red cells, and this is corrected by giving the hormone

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — bile salts: Bile salts help in the absorption of fat and have no role here

B — vitamin C in the diet: A vitamin C deficiency does not cause this anaemia

C — platelets in the blood: The platelets help in clotting and are not involved in the formation of red cells

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron alone will not correct this anaemia, since the marrow lacks the stimulus, so the prescribed erythropoietin is essential along with the iron and the vitamin supplements

question: The commonest cause of obstructive jaundice in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a stone in the common bile duct

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A stone blocking the common bile duct raises the conjugated bilirubin and produces pale stools, dark urine and itching

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — haemolysis of red cells: Haemolysis raises the unconjugated bilirubin

B — viral hepatitis: Viral hepatitis damages the liver cells and produces a mixed picture of jaundice

C — a fatty liver: A fatty liver does not by itself cause obstructive jaundice

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Pale stools with dark urine and itching point to obstruction, while an enlarged tender liver with jaundice of a mixed type suggests hepatitis, and the nurse's record of these details helps in the diagnosis
option_4: a stone in the common bile duct

question: The chief storage form of carbohydrate in the human body is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. glycogen

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The liver and the muscles join the glucose molecules into glycogen, which is broken down again when the blood sugar falls

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — starch: Starch is the storage form of carbohydrate in plants

C — glucose: Glucose is the circulating sugar and is not the storage form

D — cellulose: Cellulose is a plant fibre that human enzymes cannot digest

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

question: The desirable total blood cholesterol level in a healthy adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. below 200 milligrams per decilitre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A level below about two hundred milligrams per decilitre is taken as desirable, with the low density fraction kept low as well

A — 250 to 300 milligrams per decilitre: This range is raised and carries a risk to the heart

question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes has a blood pH of 7.2 with a low bicarbonate and deep rapid breathing. This picture is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The accumulation of ketone acids lowers the bicarbonate and the pH, and the deep rapid breathing blows off carbon dioxide as compensation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: The enzyme that is raised in the blood in diseases of the bone and in obstruction of the bile ducts is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. alkaline phosphatase

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — serum amylase: Amylase rises in acute pancreatitis

B — lactate dehydrogenase only: Lactate dehydrogenase is not specific, as it comes from many tissues

question: The correct way to give a tablet to a patient who has difficulty in swallowing is to:
solution:

question: The correct technique of giving a cleansing enema is to:

C — advise her to avoid cold food: Diet has no effect on the course of tuberculosis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The family contacts are screened and the children under five are given preventive treatment as per the programme, since one untreated case at home infects the whole household
option_1: give her a cough syrup and review her after a month
option_2: collect two sputum samples for examination, arrange a chest radiograph and referral, and explain that the treatment under the national programme is free and must be taken for the full course
option_4: send her to the district hospital without any sputum examination

question: The correct way of cleaning a blood spill on the floor of a health centre is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. wear gloves, cover the spill with an absorbent material, remove it as infectious waste and disinfect the area with a bleach solution

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The gloves protect the worker, the absorbent limits the spread and the bleach kills the organisms, including the viruses of hepatitis and HIV

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — leave it to dry by itself: A dried spill still carries the organisms and is later disturbed as dust

C — wipe it with a dry cloth and throw the cloth away: A dry cloth spreads the organisms and the cloth becomes a hazard

D — wash it away with plenty of water only: Water alone spreads the contaminated material over a wider area

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The sharps are never picked up by hand, and a brush and pan or a scoop is used, since a needle hidden in the mess is the commonest cause of a needle stick injury
option_2: wear gloves, cover the spill with an absorbent material, remove it as infectious waste and disinfect the area with a bleach solution
option_3: wipe it with a dry cloth and throw the cloth away
option_4: wash it away with plenty of water only

question: The correct action after a needle stick injury in a health worker is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. wash the area with soap and water, let it bleed gently, apply an antiseptic and a dressing, report the injury at once, and take the post exposure treatment advised after the source and the risk are assessed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Washing and gentle bleeding reduce the load of organisms, and reporting allows a proper risk assessment and prompt preventive treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — apply a tight bandage and continue working: A tight bandage does not prevent infection and the injury must still be reported

C — take no action if the needle looked clean: A used needle is never assumed to be clean, since the source patient may be unknown

D — suck the wound and cover it with cotton: Sucking the wound introduces organisms from the mouth and is not recommended

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The incident is recorded in writing on the same day, because the preventive treatment is far more effective when it is started within a few hours
option_1: apply a tight bandage and continue working
option_2: wash the area with soap and water, let it bleed gently, apply an antiseptic and a dressing, report the injury at once, and take the post exposure treatment advised after the source and the risk are assessed
option_3: take no action if the needle looked clean
option_4: suck the wound and cover it with cotton

question: The first stool passed by a newborn baby is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. meconium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Meconium is the dark green, sticky material formed from the amniotic fluid and the secretions swallowed before birth

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — dysenteric stool: A dysenteric stool contains blood and mucus and indicates infection

C — curdy stool: The curdy stool is the yellow stool of a breastfed baby after the first week

D — transitional stool: The transitional stool is the greenish brown stool passed on the third and fourth days

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The passage of meconium within the first day confirms that the bowel is patent, and its delay suggests an obstruction or a congenital problem

question: A 2-month-old infant has a weak cry, sucks poorly and has not gained weight since birth. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. examine the baby for signs of illness, ask about the feeding, look for infection or a heart problem, and refer the baby for assessment without delay

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A poor suck and a failure to gain weight are serious signs at this age and may indicate an infection, a heart defect, a metabolic problem or a feeding difficulty

🔍 Key Clues: 2-month-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — reassure the mother that all babies cry weakly at this age: Weak crying with poor weight gain is never normal

C — advise the mother to give bottle feeds in addition to breastfeeding: Changing the feeding without a diagnosis may make matters worse

D — wait until the next immunisation visit to review the baby: Waiting a month in an infant who is not thriving allows the condition to advance

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The weight is plotted on the growth chart and compared with the birth weight, as a return to the birth weight by about ten days and a steady rise afterwards are the expected pattern
option_1: examine the baby for signs of illness, ask about the feeding, look for infection or a heart problem, and refer the baby for assessment without delay
option_2: reassure the mother that all babies cry weakly at this age
option_3: advise the mother to give bottle feeds in addition to breastfeeding
option_4: wait until the next immunisation visit to review the baby

question: A 2-year-old child with wheezing is prescribed a nebulised bronchodilator. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. hold the child upright, use a properly fitting mask, ensure the drug is diluted as prescribed and give it with the prescribed flow, and observe the pulse and the breathing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The upright position, a snug mask and the correct dilution and flow deliver an adequate dose to the lungs, and observing the pulse and breathing detects both the response and the side effects

🔍 Key Clues: 2-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give the treatment while the child lies flat and cries: A crying child inhales poorly and lying flat makes the breathing harder

B — increase the flow to the maximum to shorten the treatment: An excessive flow wastes the drug and may cause tachycardia

D — use a mouthpiece as in an adult: A small child cannot use a mouthpiece effectively

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The treatment is given with the child sitting on the mother's lap, which keeps the child calm and allows the mother to be taught to give it at home
option_1: give the treatment while the child lies flat and cries
option_2: increase the flow to the maximum to shorten the treatment

question: A 62-year-old man has a serum creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL and the doctor reduces the dose of a drug that is cleared by the kidney. The part of the nephron at which this drug is filtered from the blood is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. glomerulus

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Filtration occurs at the glomerulus, where the blood pressure pushes water and small molecules into the capsule while the cells and the large proteins are held back

🔍 Key Clues: 62-year-old | 2.4 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — loop of Henle: The loop of Henle concentrates the filtrate by reabsorbing water and salts

B — distal convoluted tubule: The distal tubule exchanges ions and reabsorbs some water and salts

D — collecting duct: The collecting duct fine tunes the water and acid balance under hormonal control

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: A rising creatinine with a falling urine output is the earliest sign that the dose must be reduced, since the kidney is the main route by which many drugs and their breakdown products leave the body

question: Most drugs taken by mouth are changed in the liver before they reach the general circulation. The vessel that carries them there is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. portal vein

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The portal vein carries the blood from the intestine, loaded with the absorbed drug, to the liver for processing before it enters the general circulation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hepatic vein: The hepatic vein carries the blood away from the liver to the vena cava

C — hepatic artery: The hepatic artery supplies oxygen rich blood to the liver itself

D — inferior vena cava: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that drains the lower part of the body

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: This first pass effect is why some drugs are given under the tongue or by injection, as the whole oral dose would otherwise be reduced before it ever reaches the tissues

question: The fear of being in an open or crowded place from which escape may be difficult is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. agoraphobia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Agoraphobia is the fear of open or crowded places and of being trapped without help

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — claustrophobia: Claustrophobia is the fear of closed places

C — acrophobia: Acrophobia is the fear of heights

D — mysophobia: Mysophobia is the fear of dirt and contamination

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The person with agoraphobia often avoids going out altogether, so the nurse plans the care in small steps that begin inside the ward, because each avoided place strengthens the fear

question: A 28-year-old woman reports that for the past six months she has worried constantly about her family, her job and her health; she feels restless, cannot sleep, and her thyroid function and haemoglobin are normal. The nurse should recognise this as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a generalised anxiety disorder

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Free floating worry about many areas lasting six months or more, with restlessness and poor sleep, and with a normal physical workup, is a generalised anxiety disorder

🔍 Key Clues: 28-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a conversion disorder: A conversion disorder presents with a loss of movement or sensation that has no physical basis

C — a panic attack: A panic attack is a sudden intense episode that peaks within minutes

D — an obsessive compulsive disorder: An obsessive compulsive disorder has repeated unwanted thoughts and the acts done to relieve them

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Anxious patients are also asked about caffeine, alcohol and any over the counter remedies, because these commonly worsen the symptoms and are easy to correct

question: A patient on long term treatment for tuberculosis is advised to eat foods rich in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. vitamin B6

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The drug used in the treatment of tuberculosis can cause numbness and tingling in the limbs from a shortage of vitamin B6, so foods such as whole grains, pulses, nuts and milk are encouraged

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin C: Vitamin C helps wound healing but is not the vitamin depleted by this drug

C — vitamin K: Vitamin K is linked to clotting, not to this problem

D — sodium: Extra salt is harmful and is not advised

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The food advice is recorded and taught in the patient's own language during the first visit, since the numbness of the hands and feet is often mistaken for the disease itself

question: A junior nurse realises that she has given a drug to the wrong patient. The first action of the nurse in charge should be to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. check the patient, inform the doctor, record the incident and report it through the proper channel

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Patient safety comes first, and the incident must be recorded and reported so that the patient is watched and the system is corrected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — scold the junior nurse in front of the others: Public scolding hides the problem and stops others from reporting similar errors

B — keep quiet about the incident to protect the unit: Concealment leaves the patient unwatched and puts the whole team at risk

D — alter the record so that the mistake is not noticed: Falsifying a record is professional misconduct and is a serious offence

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The report is meant to be non punitive, since the purpose is to find why the error happened, such as similar looking labels or too many interruptions, and to remove that cause
option_1: scold the junior nurse in front of the others
option_2: keep quiet about the incident to protect the unit
option_3: check the patient, inform the doctor, record the incident and report it through the proper channel
option_4: alter the record so that the mistake is not noticed

question: A trial reports a p value of 0.04. The nurse correctly understands that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the result is statistically significant at the 5% level

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A p value below 0.05 means the difference is unlikely to have arisen by chance alone, so it is called statistically significant at the 5% level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — there is a 4% chance that the treatment works: The p value is the chance of observing such a result if the treatment truly had no effect, not the chance that the treatment works

B — the finding is due to chance: A value below 0.05 argues against chance rather than for it

C — the study proves the treatment is effective: Statistical significance does not prove clinical effectiveness, as a large study can make a tiny benefit significant

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also looks at the size of the effect and the confidence interval, because a result can be significant and still be too small to matter to the patient
option_1: there is a 4% chance that the treatment works
option_3: the study proves the treatment is effective
option_4: the result is statistically significant at the 5% level

question: The World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1980

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated in 1980 after a worldwide vaccination campaign

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1985: 1985 is later than the declaration

C — 1975: 1975 is the year the last case in Asia was recorded

D — 1970: 1970 is too early, as cases were still being reported from several countries

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Smallpox is the only human disease to have been wiped out by vaccination, which is why it is still quoted when a parent asks whether a disease can really be eliminated

question: The scheme that gives a cash incentive to a pregnant woman from a rural area to deliver her baby in a health institution is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Janani Suraksha Yojana

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Janani Suraksha Yojana gives a cash incentive to promote institutional delivery and thus reduce the maternal and newborn deaths in rural areas

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly: That programme looks after the health of elderly people

C — Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana gives a maternity benefit for the first living child, not specifically for institutional delivery

D — Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram screens children for defects and deficiencies

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The amount is paid after the delivery and the mother is also helped with the transport cost, since the aim is to remove the money barrier that keeps families from coming to the health centre
option_2: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly

question: The main purpose of Mission Indradhanush is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. expand full immunisation coverage to the children and pregnant women who are still left out

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Mission Indradhanush was launched to reach the children and pregnant women who had been missed by the routine immunisation programme and to bring their coverage up to the full schedule

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — prevent blindness in the elderly: Blindness prevention is a separate programme

B — control tuberculosis in urban slums: Tuberculosis control is the work of the national tuberculosis programme

C — eradicate polio from the country: Polio has already been eliminated and is watched for by the same programme but not run by this mission

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse doing the survey lists the unimmunised children lane by lane, as the mission works by revisiting the same area on fixed days until no child is left out
option_4: expand full immunisation coverage to the children and pregnant women who are still left out

question: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke mainly deals with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. non-communicable diseases and their common risk factors

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme addresses the four major non-communicable diseases together, because they share the same risk factors of tobacco, alcohol, unhealthy diet and lack of exercise

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only cancers of the mouth and the lung: Cancer is only one of the four diseases covered

B — communicable diseases spread by insects: Insect borne diseases belong to the communicable disease programmes

D — only diabetes among the four diseases: Diabetes alone is not the whole scope of the programme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Since the same person may be carrying more than one risk factor, the nurse records blood pressure, blood sugar and weight together in one visit instead of checking them separately
option_1: only cancers of the mouth and the lung
option_3: non-communicable diseases and their common risk factors

question: The Indian Nursing Council was set up under the Act passed in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 1947

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian Nursing Council Act was passed in 1947 to regulate nursing education and to maintain a uniform standard of training throughout the country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1949: 1949 is the year the Indian Nursing Council came into force and its first meeting was held, but the Act itself was passed earlier

B — 1952: 1952 is the year of the first nursing conference that discussed curriculum revision

D — 1950: 1950 is the year the Constitution of India came into force

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The Council's register is the reason a nurse must check that her own qualification is recognised before joining a foreign hospital, since only approved institutions are listed

question: International Nurses Day is observed every year on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 12 May

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The twelfth of May is the birthday of Florence Nightingale, and it is observed all over the world as International Nurses Day

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 24 March: The twenty fourth of March is World Tuberculosis Day

C — 1 December: The first of December is World AIDS Day

D — 7 April: The seventh of April is World Health Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The day is used to honour the work of nurses and to press for better staffing, since a shortage of nurses is itself a risk to patient safety

question: Under Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, the children are screened for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the four deficiencies, defects, diseases and developmental delay

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme screens children from birth up to eighteen years for defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies including anaemia and malnutrition, and developmental delay with disability

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — free medicines for the elderly: Medicines for the elderly come under a different programme

C — construction of household toilets: Toilet construction is part of the sanitation mission

D — pension for the disabled: Pensions are a social welfare measure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The screening is done on fixed days in the Anganwadi and the school, as the children are already there and the ones found positive are then sent for treatment free of cost
option_2: the four deficiencies, defects, diseases and developmental delay

question: The first National Health Policy of India was adopted in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1983

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The first National Health Policy of independent India was adopted in 1983 to give a direction to the health services and to aim at health for all

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1948: 1948 is the year the World Health Organization was established and the Bhore Committee reported

B — 2002: 2002 is the year of the second National Health Policy

C — 1978: 1978 is the year of the Alma Ata declaration on primary health care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The policy of 1983 is remembered for its emphasis on primary health care and on the referral system, which is why the nurse at the PHC still works within the same plan of village, sub centre and CHC

question: The percentage of oxygen in the atmosphere is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 21 per cent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Dry air contains about twenty one per cent oxygen, the gas the tissues need for respiration

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 25 per cent: Twenty five per cent is higher than the true figure

C — 16 per cent: Sixteen per cent is the level below which a flame goes out and a person becomes breathless

D — 78 per cent: Seventy eight per cent is the share of nitrogen in the air

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient whose oxygen saturation falls is given oxygen through prongs or a mask, but the flow is kept exactly as prescribed, since too much oxygen also harms a patient with a chronic lung disease

question: The vitamin needed for the clotting of blood is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. vitamin K

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin K is needed by the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors, and a shortage leads to bleeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin D: Vitamin D is needed for the absorption of calcium and for bone health

B — vitamin C: Vitamin C is needed for collagen and for the healing of wounds

D — vitamin A: Vitamin A is needed for vision and the integrity of the skin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A newborn is given vitamin K soon after birth, since the baby's gut has no bacteria yet to make it and the level of the clotting factors is low at that age

question: The instrument used to measure the arterial blood pressure is called a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sphygmomanometer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sphygmomanometer is the mercury or aneroid instrument that measures the pressure of the blood inside the artery

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — stethoscope: A stethoscope is used to hear the sounds but it does not measure the pressure

C — spirometer: A spirometer measures the volume of air breathed in and out

D — glucometer: A glucometer measures the blood sugar

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The cuff is wrapped two to three centimetres above the bend of the elbow and the arm is kept at the level of the heart, as a hanging arm reads falsely high

question: The organ that produces insulin in the human body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pancreas

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The beta cells of the islets of the pancreas make insulin, which lowers the blood sugar

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — adrenal gland: The adrenal gland makes cortisol and adrenaline

C — thyroid: The thyroid makes thyroxine, which controls the rate of metabolism

D — liver: The liver stores the sugar as glycogen but does not make insulin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient taking insulin is taught to rotate the injection site around the abdomen, because a spot used again and again becomes hard and the insulin is then absorbed unevenly

question: A deficiency of iodine in the diet causes:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. goitre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Iodine is needed to make the thyroid hormones, and its shortage makes the gland enlarge as a goitre

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rickets: Rickets results from a shortage of vitamin D

B — scurvy: Scurvy is caused by a shortage of vitamin C

D — anaemia: Anaemia is caused chiefly by a shortage of iron and of folic acid

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the salt bought in the village for the iodine content and teaches that the packet must be kept closed, since iodine is lost when the salt is stored open or heated for long

question: The SI unit of radioactivity is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. becquerel

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The becquerel is the SI unit of radioactivity and stands for one disintegration per second

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — sievert: The sievert measures the biological effect of the absorbed dose

B — roentgen: The roentgen measures the exposure to radiation

C — curie: The curie is the older unit of radioactivity and equals many becquerels

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse wears a film badge while working near the radiation source, because the badge records the dose received over time and warns the staff before the safe limit is crossed

question: Which of the following is used as a coolant in a nuclear reactor?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. heavy water

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heavy water carries away the heat produced by the reactor core and at the same time slows down the neutrons so that the chain reaction continues

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — graphite: Graphite works as a moderator in some reactors but it is not the circulating coolant

C — carbon dioxide at room temperature: Carbon dioxide is used in some gas cooled reactors but not as the standard coolant in the reactors of this country

D — liquid helium: Liquid helium is used to cool magnets, not a reactor core

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The coolant is radioactive after passing through the core, so the nurse must remember that the patient who has had a radioisotope study is kept for the advised time before the room is used for others

question: The part of the brain that controls balance and the coordination of movements is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. cerebellum

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The cerebellum lies behind the brain stem and keeps the posture and the movements smooth, which is why a patient with an injury there staggers

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cerebrum: The cerebrum is the seat of thought, memory and voluntary movement

B — medulla oblongata: The medulla controls the vital centres for breathing, heart rate and blood pressure

D — thalamus: The thalamus relays the sensory impulses to the cortex

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient with a cerebellar problem is walked with support and the bed is kept low, since the gait is unsteady and a fall is the commonest accident

question: A patient's temperature is recorded as 39 °C. Converted into the Fahrenheit scale this is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 102.2 °F

🧠 Method: The conversion is Fahrenheit equal to nine fifths of the centigrade reading plus thirty two, so 39 × 1.8 is 70.2 and adding 32 gives 102.2

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 98.6 °F: 98.6 °F is the normal body temperature and equals 37 °C

C — 100.4 °F: 100.4 °F equals 38 °C and is only a mild fever

D — 104.0 °F: 104 °F equals 40 °C

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse converts in the head to compare a reading written in another unit, but the chart must record the scale that was actually used, since a wrong conversion is a common cause of a wrong dose of an antipyretic

question: A vial contains 500 mg of a drug in 5 mL. The volume to be drawn up for a prescribed dose of 250 mg is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 2.5 mL

🧠 Method: If 5 mL holds 500 mg then each mL holds 100 mg, so 250 mg needs 2.5 mL

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 3.0 mL: 3.0 mL would give 300 mg

C — 1.5 mL: 1.5 mL would give only 150 mg

D — 5.0 mL: 5 mL is the whole vial and would double the dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The calculation is written on the chart and checked with a second nurse before a high alert drug is given, as these medicines have a narrow margin between the useful and the harmful dose

question: A nurse earns ₹18,000 a month and spends 65 per cent of it. Her monthly saving is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ₹6,300

🧠 Method: She spends 65 per cent and so saves 35 per cent, and 35 per cent of 18,000 is 6,300

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ₹5,400: ₹5,400 is 30 per cent of the income

C — ₹7,200: ₹7,200 is 40 per cent of the income

D — ₹6,000: ₹6,000 is one third of the income

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same percentage working out is used when the nurse explains to a family what share of the bill the health scheme will pay, since a family that understands the amount plans the treatment better

question: The average of five temperature readings 36, 37, 39, 40 and 38 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 38

🧠 Method: The sum is 190 and dividing by five gives 38

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 37.5: 37.5 is the value one would get by dropping the highest reading

C — 37.8: 37.8 is obtained by dividing 189 by five

D — 36.5: 36.5 is below every reading in the list except one

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The average alone never decides the care, so the nurse keeps the whole record of the readings, since a single spike that has now settled matters more than a normal average

question: A 20 per cent solution is to be diluted to a strength of 5 per cent. The ratio in which the solution must be mixed with water is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1 part of solution to 3 parts of water

🧠 Method: To bring 20 per cent down to 5 per cent the solution must be made four times its volume, so one part of the solution is mixed with three parts of water

⚡ Fast Approach: Amount of solute stays the same. Final volume = solute / final strength.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1 part of solution to 4 parts of water: One part to four parts would make the strength 4 per cent

C — 2 parts of solution to 3 parts of water: Two parts to three parts would give 8 per cent

D — 3 parts of solution to 1 part of water: Three parts of solution to one part of water would give 15 per cent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The dilution is made with the measured volume and never by eye, as a stronger solution used on a wound or on the skin can cause a burn

option_2: 1 part of solution to 3 parts of water
