question: One thousand millilitres of fluid is to be given over eight hours through a set that delivers 15 drops per millilitre. The drip rate per minute is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 31 drops

🧠 Method: The total drops are 1,000 × 15 which is 15,000, and over eight hours there are 480 minutes, so 15,000 divided by 480 gives about 31 drops a minute

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 25 drops: 25 drops a minute would take about ten hours

C — 21 drops: 21 drops a minute would run the bottle in about twelve hours

D — 41 drops: 41 drops a minute would finish the bottle in about six hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The rate is counted for a full minute with a watch and recorded every hour, since an infusion that runs too fast can overload the circulation, especially in a child or an elderly patient

question: An article is sold for ₹650 at a profit of 30 per cent. Its cost price was:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ₹500

🧠 Method: If the cost price is 100 then the selling price at a profit of 30 per cent is 130, and 650 divided by 130 and multiplied by 100 gives 500

⚡ Fast Approach: Profit percent is always on the cost price, loss percent also on the cost price.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ₹520: ₹520 gives a profit of 25 per cent

C — ₹455: ₹455 is 70 per cent of the selling price

D — ₹480: ₹480 gives a profit of about 35 per cent

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The same proportion sum is used when a patient compares the price of a medicine bought loose with the price of the same medicine in a strip, as the strip is usually the cheaper of the two

question: Which letter comes next in the series A, C, F, J, O?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. U

🧠 Method: The gaps between the letters grow by one each time, being two, three, four and five, so the next gap is six and O plus six places gives U

⚡ Fast Approach: Number the letters A=1 to Z=26 and work with numbers instead of letters.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — S: S would mean a gap of only four places

B — T: T would mean a gap of five places, which has already been used

C — V: V would jump seven places

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out a pattern step by step is the same discipline the nurse uses on a fluid balance chart, where each entry must be read against the one before it rather than in isolation

question: The next number in the series 3, 6, 11, 18, 27 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 38

🧠 Method: The differences are 3, 5, 7 and 9, so the next difference is 11 and 27 plus 11 gives 38

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 36: 36 would come from adding 9 again

C — 40: 40 would come from adding 13

D — 35: 35 would come from adding 8

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Looking for the pattern behind a set of figures is the same habit the nurse uses on a chart, where a steady rise in the pulse over three readings means more than any single value

question: If each letter is replaced by its position in the English alphabet, the word NURSE is written as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 14-21-18-19-5

🧠 Method: N is the fourteenth letter, U the twenty first, R the eighteenth, S the nineteenth and E the fifth

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 14-21-17-19-5: The position of R is written short by one

B — 15-22-19-20-6: Each number is one more than the true position

D — 13-20-17-18-4: Each number is one less than the true position

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same careful matching of a symbol to a value is what keeps the nurse safe while comparing a drug label with the prescription, since a single transposed figure changes the dose

question: In a row of 40 school children a girl is twelfth from the left end. Her position from the right end is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 29th

🧠 Method: The position from the right is the total number of children plus one minus the position from the left, so 40 plus 1 minus 12 gives 29

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 27th: 27th is got by subtracting 13 from 40

C — 30th: 30th is got by subtracting 10 from 40

D — 28th: 28th is got by subtracting 12 from 40

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same simple sum is used while arranging the queue for the immunisation camp, as the nurse must know how many children are still waiting before the vaccine vial is opened

question: Which of the following numbers is the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 200, 225?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 200

🧠 Method: All the others are perfect squares of whole numbers, namely eleven, twelve, thirteen and fifteen, while 200 is not

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 169: 169 is the square of thirteen

B — 144: 144 is the square of twelve

C — 121: 121 is the square of eleven

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Spotting the one value that does not fit the pattern is exactly what the nurse does when a single reading in a series looks out of line, and it is then repeated before any action is taken

question: A man walks 3 kilometres towards the north and then 4 kilometres towards the east. How far is he from the starting point?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 5 kilometres

🧠 Method: The two paths are at right angles and form a right angled triangle, so the distance is the square root of three squared plus four squared, which is the square root of twenty five, that is five

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 7 kilometres: Seven is the sum of the two distances

C — 6 kilometres: Six would mean the paths added simply

D — 4 kilometres: Four ignores the northward walk

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse uses the same sense of direction and distance while planning a home visit round, so that the maximum number of homes is covered in the shortest possible walk

question: Between four o'clock and five o'clock, at what time do the two hands of a clock come together?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 4 hours and about 22 minutes

🧠 Method: The hands come together a little after twenty minutes past four, at about four hours and twenty two minutes, since the minute hand gains on the hour hand in the interval

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 4 hours and about 16 minutes: At four sixteen the minute hand is still behind the hour hand

B — 4 hours 25 minutes: At four twenty five the minute hand is already ahead of the hour hand

D — 4 hours 20 minutes: At exactly four twenty the minute hand is at four but the hour hand has moved past four

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same estimation of a short interval is used while timing a contraction or a pulse, where the nurse counts for a full minute unless the rhythm is known to be regular
